title: Dragon Force
subtitle: The armies of Legendra
summary: Dragon Force is J-Force and Sega's strategy role-playing game, first released for Saturn in Japan on 29 March 1996.
body: Dragon Force is J-Force and Sega's strategy role-playing game, first released for Saturn in Japan on 29 March 1996. The player leads one of Legendra's rulers, moving armies between castles while the continent faces a returning ancient threat. Each general can command up to a hundred soldiers, allowing two hundred figures to meet in a single battle. Those encounters give the campaign its striking spectacle, but the journey also depends on recruiting officers, supporting their growth and deciding where each force will be needed next.

When opposing armies meet, the game moves from the map to a battlefield. The player chooses a general, troops and a formation after seeing the enemy's selection, creating an opportunity to answer that force with a suitable arrangement. Soldiers fight in real time, while menus allow orders and special attacks to interrupt the action. Defeating a general can capture or injure an opponent. If both sides lose their soldiers, the remaining commanders may end the encounter in a duel, making the officers important beyond the size of their armies.

Between campaigns, administrative periods let the ruler reward generals, recruit new officers, persuade prisoners to join and strengthen castles. Rewards can increase an officer's troop capacity, so a useful commander becomes more valuable through service. Different rulers begin with their own circumstances and followers, giving another campaign a different route across the same continent. Working Designs translated the North American edition, later used for the European release. Dragon Force connects its crowded battles to these quieter decisions, allowing the army on screen to reflect relationships and preparations made on the map.
